chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Bakr, from Salih, from Suleyman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no one in the stage of childhood who commits to reciting every night: "Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of Al-Falaq" and "Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of the people", each one three times, and "Say: He is Allah, One" one hundred times; and if he is not able, then fifty times, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will divert from him every mental affliction or illness from the illnesses of children, and dangerous thirst, and spoilage of the stomach, and blood circulation disorders, forever, as long as he maintains this vow until he reaches old age.'
So if he commits himself to that, or maintains it, he will be protected until the Day Allah, Mighty and Majestic, captures his soul.

key_terms.قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ: Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of the people (Surah 114)
key_terms.قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ: Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of Al-Falaq (Surah 113)

ai.seo_question: What nightly Quranic recitation protects children from illness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records Imam al-Rida (AS) prescribing a nightly regimen of reciting Al-Falaq, An-Nas, and Al-Ikhlas to safeguard children from 'lamam' (minor distractions or ailments) and physical disorders like stomach issues and thirst. This practice, rooted in the concept of 'tawqif' (divine instruction), ensures continuous protection until old age, reflecting the Shia emphasis on utilizing Quranic recitation as a means of spiritual and physical preservation (hifz) for the young.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Bakr, from Salih, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘There is no one (still) in the limit of childhood who vows for the recitation during every night with [113:1] Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of Al Falaq (Chapter 113) and [114:1] Say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of the people (Chapter 114), each one three times, and [112:1] Say: He Allah is One one-hundred times, but if he is not able, then fifty times, except that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Exchange from him, every mental problem, or an illness from the illnesses of the children, and the dangerous thirst (dehydration), and the spoiling of the stomach, and the blood circulation (disorder), ever, for as long as he vows by this until he reaches the old age.
So if he were to vow himself with that, or keeps on vowing, would be protected up to the Day Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Captures his soul’.
en.sarwar: 17. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Bakr from Salih from Sulayman al-Ja’fari who has said the following: “I heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) saying, ‘

If a child maintains reading every night Chapters 113, 114 three times each and Chapter 112 one hundred times or, if he cannot do it, fifty times Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, diverts all health problems of childhood and dehydration, stomach disorder and blood pressure all the time, as long as he maintains such readings until his old age.
If he would maintain it or is made to maintain it, he will remain safe until the time Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will take his soul away.’”
